full_judgment:
9. Mr Khurshid Alam Khan, learned Advocate, appearing for the accused-appellant, has made submissions in the light of the leave granting. order. He has drawn our attention to the provisions of sections 11 (ka) and 11 (ga) of the Ain, 2000 and has submitted that in maintaining the order of conviction and sentence passed by the Tribunal, the High Court Division totally failed to consider that the evidence adduced by the prosecution at best attract section 11 (ga) of the Ain, 2000 and as such, the order of conviction of the accused under section 11 (ka) thereof and the sentence awarded thereunder by the Tribunal as affirmed by the High Court Division cannot be maintained and the same be set aside. Advisedly, he did not, however, argue for a clean acquittal of the accused of the charge brought against him. 

 10. Mr Biswajit Deb Nath, learned Deputy Attorney-General, appearing for the State, has contended that PW 1 (the informant) has clearly stated in his evidence that the victim was 8( eight) months pregnant at the time of occurrence and the accused assaulted her with lathi which had been corroborated 'by the other PWs. The injuries sustained by the victim can be easily termed to be 'grievous hurt' within the meaning of clause- 'Eighthly' of section 320 of the Penal Code though the doctor certified that the injuries suffered by her were simple in nature. Therefore, the High Court Division did not commit any illegality in maintaining the order of conviction and sentence of the Tribunal and there being no merit in the appeal, the same be dismissed. 

 12.From the judgment and order of the Tribunal, it appears that it found the accused guilty under section 11(ka) of the Ain, 2000 on the finding, inter alia, that the evidence of the PWs proved that on the date of occurrence, i.e. on 26-8-2000, the accused had been at the house of PW 1, i.e. the victim's father who paid Taka 10,000 as part payment of the remaining dowry, there was altercation between them over the non-payment of full dowry and at one point of time, the accused severely assaulted his wife, the victim with a lathi "who was then 8(eight) months pregnant" and because of the result of "severe beating" the victim gave birth to a child in the night following 26-8-2000. 

 14. From the judgment of the Tribunal, it further appears that it did not give any specific finding that the evidence on record proved the charge leveled against the accused under section 11 (ka) of the Ain, 2000 or the evidence on record at all attracted the provision of section 11(ka) of the Ain, 2000 and accordingly warranted the conviction of the accused under the said section of the Ain, 2000. The Tribunal after discussing the evidence on record abruptly ordered that the accused "is found guilty under section 11(ka) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 and he is convicted and sentenced to suffer rigorous (sic) imprisonment for life along with a fine of Taka 50,000 (fifty thousand)" and the other order as stated herein before. The High Court Division also made the same mistake. In the context, it needs to be mentioned that from the impugned judgment and order, it does not appear that argument was advanced before the High Court Division that all the injuries inflicted upon the victim being simple in nature, section 11 (ka) had no manner of application and therefore, the conviction under the said section was bad. 

 (i)মারাত্মক জখম (grievous hurt) and (ii) সাধারণ জখম (simple hurt)to be caused to a ‘নারী’ for dowry and has also prescribed separate punishments for causing such hurts as specified in clauses (kha) and (ga) thereof. In the context, it needs to be mentioned that whatever may be the nature of the injuries sustained by the victim, there is ample evidence that the injuries were caused to the victim for dowry. 

 17. Clause (ka) of section 11 does not speak of any hurt grievous or simple, it has prescribed two kinds of punishments (i) sentence of death if anyone causes the death of a ‘নারী’ for dowry and (ii) imprisonment for life if anyone attempts to cause death of a ‘নারী’ for dowry and in both the cases, fine has to be also imposed. So, in order to convict a person and to sentence him under clause-(ka) of section 11, there must be evidence that a person so charged either caused death of a ‘নারী’ or attempted to cause death of a. Therefore, we need to look at the evidence on record and see whether the accused at all attempted to cause death of the victim and whether section 11 (ka) of the Ain, 2000 is attracted. 

 22. Admittedly, the victim gave birth to a child at 3 o'clock in the night following the date of the occurrence and none of the PWs said that because of the assault by the accused, the victim .experienced any physical discomfort or complications in giving birth to the child or the child was born with any abnormality or with any hurt or with any other disability. When the victim herself has categorically stated that the accused only throttled her; it is very difficult to accept the evidence of the other PWs that she was assaulted by the accused with a lathi on any part of her body, or the belly as stated by PW 8. If really, the accused had struck at the belly of the victim with a lathi as stated by PW 8, then something very serious or dangerous to her life would have happened, because the very fact that the accused gave birth to a child at 3 o’clock in the night following the date of occurrence, prima facie, shows that she was at the advance stage of her pregnancy, though she did not say in her testimony about the period of her pregnancy. The very fact that though the accused allegedly assaulted the victim at 8-30/9-00 am, the doctor examined her at 5-00 pm, on being called in, prima facie shows that nothing serious or dangerous to the life of the victim happened and, in fact, the alleged assault by the victim had no effect or impact upon her body and caused no difficulty to give birth to the child. The medical certificate issued by PW 10 shows that all the injuries allegedly sustained by the victim were simple in nature. It is true that the opinion of a doctor who examines a victim as to whether a hurt is simple or grievous is not conclusive; the view of the doctor furnishes the Court a clue to the question. Four injuries have been mentioned in the medical certificate (Exhibit-4) and of these injuries, only injury No.1 corresponds to the testimony of PW 2; the victim and all the injuries have been described as simple in nature. However, we find it difficult to accept the evidence of the other PWs that the accused assaulted the victim with lathi or struck at her belly with lathi in view of the testimony of PW 2 and, therefore, to accept the other injuries, namely, injury Nos.2, 3 and 4. 

 26. The evidence of the PWs discussed hereinbefore do not at all attract clauses 'First to Seventh'. The learned Deputy Attorney-General did not also argue that the evidence on record attract any of those clauses. So, clause 'Eighthly' is left only. 

 27. In this clause, there are 3(three) expressions; (a) any hurt which endangers life or (b) which causes the sufferer to be during the space of twenty days, in severe bodily pain or (c) unable to follow his ordinary pursuits. The second and the third expressions are not also attracted in the instant case as the evidence on record do not show that the victim suffered severe bodily pain for a period of twenty days from the date of occurrence or she was unable to follow her ordinary pursuits for the said period. So, the first expression is left only. And the question to be decided precisely is whether throttling of the victim, who was at a fairly advanced stage of pregnancy, can be grouped within the phrase 'endangers life'. 

 31. The question whether the injuries suffered by the victim were dangerous to life is relevant, but what is more relevant is how far it had placed the victim in danger of her life. From the medical certificate (Exhibit-4) and the evidence of the doctor (PW 10), it appears that the victim allegedly sustained 4(four) injuries. The doctor has described the injuries including the injury caused due to throttling as simple in nature and none of the injuries had put the life of the victim in imminent danger of her life. At the risk of repetition, it is stated that the very fact that the doctor was called in to examine the, victim at 5-00 pm, the occurrence having taken place at 8-30-9-00 am, also proves that the injuries allegedly caused upon the victim by the accused were not imminently dangerous and those did not endanger her life either at the time of assault or thereafter; she could give birth to a child in a normal manner at the house of her father. Surely, we would have found substance in the submission of the learned Deputy Attorney, had it been a case that because of the throttling of the victim by the accused, who was at an advance stage of her pregnancy, there was any impact upon her body and she was put in imminent danger of her life and thus, endangering her life, but nothing happened. Not only that, there was no physical complication in giving birth to the child as well. None of the PWs stated that the victim suffered from any physical complications after the birth of the child too. So, by no means or logic, it can be said that the act of throttling by the accused as alleged by the victim (PW 2), who was at the advanced stage of pregnancy, can be construed as an attempt to cause her death within the meaning of clause (ka) of section 11 of the Ain, 2000 as argued by the learned Deputy Attorney-General. 

 32. From the judgment of the Tribunal and the High Court Division, it appears that both of them gave finding that the child was born because of the severe beating by the accused without sifting and scanning the evidence on record and, in fact, they were swayed and moved by the fact that the child was born after the incident. Both the Tribunal and the High Court Division failed to consider the testimony of PW 2 (the victim) that the accused allegedly throttled her only; the doctor was called in for her treatment after 8(eight) hours of the occurrence and that the victim gave birth to a child at 3 o’clock in the night, following the date of occurrence, i.e. after 18 hours and did not also care to consider whether the act of throttling by the accused at all falls within the phrase grievous hurt and thus fell into an error in finding the accused guilty under section 11(ka) of the Ain, 2000. Therefore, the order of conviction of the accused under section 11 (ka) of the Ain, 2000 and the sentence awarded thereunder cannot be sustained.
